Introduction

Be'O, born Yoo Chan-wook, is a South Korean rapper and songwriter known for his emotive lyricism and distinct vocal tone. Raised in Jongno District, Seoul, he developed an interest in hip hop after watching Show Me the Money 3, which inspired him to pursue a music career from his middle school years. He later graduated from the School of Performing Arts Seoul and gained early performance experience through his appearance on High School Rapper 3. His stage name “Be'O” is derived from his Christian name, Pio.

He officially began his career in 2020 after signing with the hip hop label FameUs Entertainment, founded by rapper San E. That year, he participated in the label’s compilation albums God FameUs and Famous FameUs before making his solo debut with the single “Monster.” He continued to build momentum with the release of “Bipolar” in 2021, showcasing his evolving artistry and emotional depth.

Be'O rose to mainstream prominence through his appearance on Show Me the Money 10 in 2021, where he became one of the breakout stars of the season. His performances on the show, including tracks like “Breathe,” “Limousine,” “MBTI,” and “Without You,” gained significant attention, with several of the songs topping the Gaon Digital Chart. He ultimately finished the show in third place, further solidifying his presence in the Korean hip hop scene. In December of that same year, he released the chart-topping single “Counting Stars” featuring Beenzino, which further elevated his popularity.

Following his rise to fame, Be’O expanded his activities and signed a co-management deal with BPM Entertainment while remaining under FameUs. Around this time, he was also appointed as the brand ambassador for Kappa. In September 2022, he released his first extended play Five Senses, further showcasing his versatility and musical identity. In 2024, he returned with his second extended play Affection, continuing to explore personal and introspective themes through his music.
